about: Steps 19a and 23a: money by place and year for the whole world. See worldfill/build_money_table.py and worldfill/money_world.py for the rules. Notes are for developers only; the game never shows them.

currencies.name: goods to trade
currencies.note: No money: people swap goods. Amounts are hundredths of a day of work and show as goods worth about N days of work.

currencies.name: weighed silver
currencies.note: 1 shekel = 180 grains (se), 1 mina = 60 shekels. Laws of Hammurabi 273: a hired labourer 6 grains of silver a day in the first five months of the year, 5 grains after. Held flat for the whole period.

currencies.name: copper by weight
currencies.note: 1 deben = 10 kite (qedet). Deir el-Medina workmen (New Kingdom) got about 5.5 khar of grain a month; a khar of emmer cost about 2 copper deben: about 11 deben a month, near 4 kite a day.

currencies.name: Greek drachma
currencies.note: 1 drachma = 6 obols = 48 chalkoi (Athens). Erechtheion accounts 409-406 BCE: 1 drachma a day for skilled and unskilled alike; Eleusis accounts 329 BCE: unskilled 1.5 drachmae. -600 is a guess.

currencies.name: Roman denarius
currencies.note: From 141 BCE 1 denarius = 4 sestertii = 16 asses; 1 aureus = 25 denarii (regular from Caesar). Cicero (Pro Roscio Comoedo): a labourer 12 asses a day; Matthew 20: a denarius a day. Later anchors are guesses (the 3rd-century debasement is not modelled).

currencies.name: Byzantine solidus
currencies.note: 6th-7th c.: 1 solidus = 12 miliaresia = 288 folles. A labourer near 1/24 solidus a day: a guess.

currencies.name: dirham
currencies.note: Gold dinar, silver dirham, copper fals. The dinar was 10 dirhams early and 20 or more later; 20 is used. 24 fulus to the dirham and a dirham a day for a labourer are guesses.

currencies.name: Persian toman
currencies.note: Safavid-Qajar money of account: 1 toman = 50 abbasi = 200 shahi = 10,000 dinar. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Ottoman akçe
currencies.note: Ottoman silver akce; para = 3 akce (from the 1620s), kurus = 40 para (from 1688). Unskilled wages near 3 akce (1450) and 6 (1550) are rough; later anchors follow the debasements, roughly.

currencies.name: Ottoman kuruş
currencies.note: From 1844: 1 lira = 100 kurus, 1 kurus = 40 para. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: pound sterling
currencies.note: 1 pound = 20 shillings = 240 pence = 960 farthings. An English building labourer's day: about 1.5d (1260s), 3-4d after the Black Death, 8d (1600), 12d (1650s); later anchors rough.

currencies.name: pound sterling
currencies.note: Decimal pound from 15 February 1971. Wages are guesses (an unskilled day).

currencies.name: French livre
currencies.note: 1 livre = 20 sous = 240 deniers. A Paris labourer near 20 sous a day in 1789; earlier anchors rough.

currencies.name: French franc
currencies.note: Franc = 100 centimes (old francs until 1959). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: French franc
currencies.note: New franc (100 old) from 1960. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: thaler
currencies.note: 1 thaler = 24 groschen = 288 pfennigs (Saxon reckoning; it varied by state). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: German mark
currencies.note: Mark = 100 pfennigs (Reichsmark from 1924; the 1923 inflation is not modelled). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Deutsche Mark
currencies.note: Deutsche Mark from June 1948. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Spanish peso
currencies.note: Peso (piece of eight) = 8 reales; 1 real = 34 maravedis (1497). Wages are rough guesses.

currencies.name: copper cash
currencies.note: Round copper cash (wen); 1,000 cash on a string; the silver tael near 1,000 cash (it went from about 700 to 2,000). Song common labourer near 100 cash a day; the rest are guesses.

currencies.name: Chinese yuan
currencies.note: Republican silver dollar (yuan) = 100 fen (the 1940s inflation is not modelled). Guesses.

currencies.name: Chinese yuan
currencies.note: Renminbi yuan = 10 jiao = 100 fen. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Japanese mon
currencies.note: Copper mon, 1,000 to the kan (a string). Wages were told in mon; the gold ryo (officially 4,000 mon from 1601; markets varied) is left out. Wages are guesses (an Edo labourer near 200-300 mon).

currencies.name: Japanese yen
currencies.note: Yen = 100 sen (sen out of use from 1953). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: US dollar
currencies.note: US dollar = 100 cents. An unskilled day; guesses.

currencies.name: Russian ruble
currencies.note: Ruble = 100 kopeks (1535 reform). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: cacao beans
currencies.note: Cacao beans as small change (Aztec, early colonial); a load (carga) = 24,000 beans. A day's pay of about 100 beans is a guess.

currencies.name: cowrie shells
currencies.note: Cowrie shells as money in West Africa; they lost value as more were shipped in. Guesses.

currencies.name: pana
currencies.note: Arthashastra: 1 pana = 16 mashakas, 1 mashaka = 4 kakanis; the lowest servants 60 panas a year (about 1/6 pana a day). Kept as the money of account after the Mauryas: a simplification.

currencies.name: tanka
currencies.note: Delhi Sultanate silver tanka = 48 copper jitals (Iltutmish). A day's pay of 2 jitals is a guess (Akbar's 2 dams were about 2.4 jitals).

currencies.name: hun
currencies.note: Gold hun (pagoda, varaha), fanam and copper kasu (cash). Ratios varied by place (later Madras: 42 fanams to the pagoda); 10 fanams and 16 kasu are simplifications. Half a fanam a day is a guess.

currencies.name: Mughal rupee
currencies.note: Sher Shah's rupiya and dam; Ain-i-Akbari (1595): 1 rupee = 40 dams, 1 dam = 25 jitals (of account); an ordinary labourer 2 dams a day. Later anchors are guesses.

currencies.name: sicca rupee
currencies.note: Rupee = 16 annas = 192 pai, as the Deccan, the Marathas and Bengal reckoned in the 1700s. Wages are guesses (1-2 annas a day).

currencies.name: Hali sicca
currencies.note: Hyderabad's Hali sicca rupee (from 1858), 16 annas of 12 pai. Wages are guesses (2-4 annas).

currencies.name: Osmania sicca
currencies.note: Hyderabad's Osmania sicca 1918-1959: rupee = 16 annas = 192 pai; from 1950 with the Indian rupee at 7 O.S. = 6 Indian rupees; demonetised 1959. Agricultural Labour Enquiry 1950-51: casual men earned 16 annas a day in the south and 13 in central India (Indian rupees; 13.7 Indian annas = 16 O.S. annas). 1948 = 16 annas is the design anchor (a paper 1 anna, a map 8 annas); the other anchors are guesses.

currencies.name: Indian rupee
currencies.note: Company rupee from 1835, British Indian rupee, then India's rupee until 1956: 1 rupee = 16 annas = 64 pice = 192 pies. Agricultural Labour Enquiry 1950-51: 17.5 annas a day for casual men, all India. Earlier anchors are guesses.

currencies.name: Indian rupee
currencies.note: Decimal rupee from 1 April 1957: 100 naye paise (just paise from 1964). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Indian rupee
currencies.note: Rupee = 100 paise. A rural labourer's day; guesses.

currencies.name: silver and copper coins
currencies.note: Fallback where coins were used but no row says which: no coin names are claimed, and amounts show as coins worth N days of work (hundredths of a day).

currencies.name: local money
currencies.note: Fallback after 1800 where no row names the money: no names are claimed, and amounts show as local money worth N days of work (hundredths of a day).

currencies.name: Italian lira
currencies.note: Lira = 100 centesimi (Napoleonic lira from 1807, Sardinian lira from 1816, Italian lira 1861-2001; centesimi gone after the war). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Neapolitan ducat
currencies.note: Kingdom of Naples and the Two Sicilies: ducat = 10 carlini = 100 grana. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Papal scudo
currencies.note: Papal States: scudo = 100 baiocchi (decimal from 1835; 10 paoli before). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Portuguese real
currencies.note: Real (plural reis), 1435-1911; the tostao of 100 reis, the vintem of 20, the mil-reis of 1,000 as the counting unit. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Portuguese escudo
currencies.note: Escudo = 100 centavos (1,000 reis), 1911-2001. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: East German mark
currencies.note: Mark of the GDR, 1948-1990. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: gulden
currencies.note: Habsburg and south German gulden of 60 kreuzer (Conventionsgulden from 1753). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Austro-Hungarian gulden
currencies.note: Austrian gulden (forint) of 100 kreuzer, 1857-1892. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Austrian schilling
currencies.note: Schilling = 100 groschen, 1925-1938 and 1945-2001. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Dutch guilder
currencies.note: Guilder = 20 stuivers = 160 duits (the Low Countries and the VOC). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Dutch guilder
currencies.note: Decimal guilder = 100 cents, 1817-2001. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Belgian franc
currencies.note: Belgian franc = 100 centimes, 1832-2001. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Luxembourg franc
currencies.note: At par with the Belgian franc from 1921. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Swiss franc
currencies.note: Swiss franc = 100 rappen (centimes), from 1850. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Danish rigsdaler
currencies.note: Rigsdaler = 6 mark = 96 skilling (Denmark-Norway; rigsbankdaler from 1813). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Danish krone
currencies.note: Krone = 100 ore, from 1875 (Greenland and the Faroes too). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Norwegian krone
currencies.note: Krone = 100 ore, from 1875. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Swedish daler
currencies.note: Daler = 4 mark = 32 ore, 1534-1776 (silver and copper daler are not told apart). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Swedish krona
currencies.note: Krona = 100 ore, from 1873. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Czechoslovak koruna
currencies.note: After the 1953 reform, to 1992. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Yugoslav dinar
currencies.note: Convertible dinar 1990 onwards; the 1992-1994 hyperinflation and the 1994 dinar are not followed.

currencies.name: Greek drachma
currencies.note: After 1944 (the 1944 and 1954 changes are not told apart; the 1944-1953 inflation is not followed).

currencies.name: Bulgarian lev
currencies.note: New lev (1,000 old) 1999-2025; the euro from 1 January 2026.

currencies.name: Cypriot pound
currencies.note: Decimal pound: 1,000 mils (100 cents from 1983), 1955-2007, then the euro. Guesses.

currencies.name: Frankish denier
currencies.note: Merovingian and Carolingian silver penny; pound and shilling as counting units from Charlemagne's reform. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: pfennig
currencies.note: The penny of the German lands, Bohemia and the Low Countries before the thaler; groschen from about 1300 (Prague 1300), the Rhenish gulden from 1354 (both changed a lot against the penny). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Italian lira of account
currencies.note: Lira = 20 soldi = 240 denari, the counting money of the Italian states (Venice, Genoa, Milan, Florence and the rest; their gold ducats and florins changed against it). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Portuguese dinheiro
currencies.note: 1147-1434, before the real. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Castilian maravedí
currencies.note: Maravedi = 10 dineros in Castile and Leon before the 1497 reform (the gold dobla changed against it). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Aragonese diner
currencies.note: Lliura = 20 sous = 240 diners. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: weighed silver
currencies.note: Viking-age silver by weight (hacksilver, rings, cut coins): mark = 8 ore = 24 ortugar. A day's work near a third of an ortug (2-3 grams) is a guess.

currencies.name: Scandinavian mark
currencies.note: Medieval Danish, Norwegian and Swedish counting: mark = 8 ore = 24 ortugar = 240 penninge (the Swedish mark had 192). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: homespun cloth (vaðmál)
currencies.note: Icelandic and Norse Greenland money of account: ells of homespun wool cloth; a hundred = 120 ells (a cow's worth). A day's work near 2 ells is a guess.

currencies.name: Polish denar
currencies.note: Silver penny of the Piast kingdom; the grzywna (mark) as counting unit. Guesses.

currencies.name: Polish grosz
currencies.note: Krakow grosz from 1338 (18 denars), the zloty of 30 groszy as counting unit from 1496. Guesses.

currencies.name: Hungarian denár
currencies.note: Silver denar from Stephen I; the gold forint (florin) from 1325, near 100 denars. Guesses.

currencies.name: Serbian medieval dinar
currencies.note: Perper (counting unit) = 12 dinars. A dinar a day is a guess.

currencies.name: Rus' grivna
currencies.note: Grivna of silver (ingots) = 25 kunas = 50 rezanas = 150 vekshas (Russkaya Pravda). A rezana a day is a guess.

currencies.name: Muscovite denga
currencies.note: Silver denga from the 1380s; ruble (counting) = 200 dengas. Guesses.

currencies.name: Maltese scudo
currencies.note: Knights of Malta: scudo = 12 tari = 240 grani. Guesses.

currencies.name: Bukharan tanga
currencies.note: Timurid and Uzbek silver tanga; the gold tilla near 21 tangas, the copper pul 64 to the tanga (it varied by khanate and time). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Persian siglos
currencies.note: Achaemenid gold daric = 20 silver sigloi; a siglos near a Babylonian shekel (180 grains); small sums in weighed silver. A day's work near 6-8 grains of silver, as in Babylon.

currencies.name: Persian drachm
currencies.note: Parthian and Sasanian silver drachm (and Sogdian, Chorasmian and Kushan coins of that standard), 6 obols; copper below. Half a drachm a day is a guess.

currencies.name: Carthaginian shekel
currencies.note: Punic silver shekel; 24 bronze pieces to it is a guess, as is the day's pay.

currencies.name: Aksumite coin
currencies.note: Aksumite gold, silver and bronze coins (about 270-700). The ratio is a guess.

currencies.name: Maria Theresa thaler
currencies.note: The Austrian silver thaler (dated 1780) that was the money of Ethiopia, Arabia and the Red Sea into the 20th century; 16 gersh (piastres) to it as in Ethiopia (it varied). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: salt bars (amole)
currencies.note: Ethiopian bars of rock salt used as money (5 to 8 to the thaler in the 1800s). Two bars a day is a guess.

currencies.name: Egyptian pound
currencies.note: Pound = 100 piastres (1,000 milliemes from 1885; 40 para to the piastre before). Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Sudanese dinar
currencies.note: 1992-2007 (10 old pounds to the dinar). Guesses.

currencies.name: Tunisian franc
currencies.note: At par with the French franc, 1891-1958. Guesses.

currencies.name: Algerian budju
currencies.note: Regency of Algiers: budju = 24 muzunas. Guesses.

currencies.name: Algerian franc
currencies.note: At par with the French franc, 1848-1959. Guesses.

currencies.name: Moroccan mithqal
currencies.note: Mithqal = 10 uqiya = 40 muzunas (it fell over time). Guesses.

currencies.name: Syrian pound
currencies.note: From 1919 (shared with Lebanon to 1939; the collapse after 2011 roughly). Guesses.

currencies.name: Saudi riyal
currencies.note: Hejazi and Saudi riyal of 22 ghirsh, to 1959. Guesses.

currencies.name: East African shilling
currencies.note: East Africa, Aden, Somaliland, Eritrea and Ethiopia in the war years: shilling = 100 cents. Guesses.

currencies.name: Gulf rupee
currencies.note: Indian rupee issued for the Gulf, 1959-1966. Guesses.

currencies.name: Iranian rial
currencies.note: From 1932 (dinars not in use; prices are told in tomans of 10 rials in speech). Guesses.

currencies.name: manillas
currencies.note: Brass and copper bracelets used as money in the Niger Delta and the Bight of Biafra until 1949. Guesses.

currencies.name: nzimbu shells
currencies.note: Olivancillaria shells from Luanda island, the money of the Kongo kingdom (counted in thousands); the lufuku of 10,000 and a day's pay are guesses.

currencies.name: cut silver (ariary)
currencies.note: Merina Madagascar: silver dollars (ariary) cut into pieces and weighed; a voamena = 1/24 ariary (the pieces went down to 1/720). Guesses.

currencies.name: French colonial franc
currencies.note: The French franc in the African colonies before the CFA franc (local coins and notes at par). Guesses.

currencies.name: CFA franc
currencies.note: West and Central African CFA francs (at par with each other), from December 1945. Guesses.

currencies.name: Malagasy ariary
currencies.note: Ariary = 5 iraimbilanja (= 5 old francs), sole money from 2005.

currencies.name: West African pound
currencies.note: Sterling coins, then the West African Currency Board's pound (1913-1968). Guesses.

currencies.name: Gambian dalasi
currencies.note: From 1971 (the Gambian pound 1964-1971 is not told apart). Guesses.

currencies.name: Liberian dollar
currencies.note: 1847-1907 and from 1982 (the US dollar in between). Guesses.

currencies.name: Zaire
currencies.note: 1967-1997 (the 1990s hyperinflation and the 1993 new zaire are not followed).

currencies.name: Rwandan franc
currencies.note: Rwanda-Burundi franc 1960-1964, then the Rwandan franc. Guesses.

currencies.name: Ethiopian birr
currencies.note: Ethiopian dollar (birr in Amharic) from 1945. Guesses.

currencies.name: Somali shilling
currencies.note: From 1962 (the shilling fell far; dollars took over). Guesses.

currencies.name: Rhodesian pound
currencies.note: Southern Rhodesian, Federation and Rhodesian pounds, 1939-1970. Guesses.

currencies.name: Zimbabwean dollar
currencies.note: 1980-2008 (the 2006-2008 hyperinflation and its new dollars are not followed).

currencies.name: Comorian franc
currencies.note: Madagascar-Comoros franc, then the Comorian franc (1981). Guesses.

currencies.name: Ceylon rixdollar
currencies.note: Dutch and early British Ceylon, to 1827. Guesses.

currencies.name: Ceylon rupee
currencies.note: Ceylon rupee from 1872 (Sri Lankan rupee from 1972). Guesses.

currencies.name: Nepalese mohur
currencies.note: Silver mohur of 128 dams; the copper paisa of 4 dams (fixed only in 1903, when the mohur became 50 paisa). Replaced at 2 mohurs to the rupee in 1932. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Bhutanese ngultrum
currencies.note: From 1974 (at par with the Indian rupee).

currencies.name: cowrie shells
currencies.note: The Maldives shipped cowries to half the world and used them at home. Guesses.

currencies.name: Burmese silver kyat
currencies.note: Silver by weight (a kyat near 16 grams): 1 kyat = 4 mat = 8 mu = 16 pe = 64 pya; coins of the same units from 1852 to 1889. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Tibetan tangka
currencies.note: Silver weighed in srang (taels) and counted in sho and skar; the tangka coin = 15 skar = 1.5 sho (struck from 1763), the srang coin from 1909. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: silver by weight
currencies.note: Silver weighed in taels (liang), mace (qian) and candareens (fen): Mongol ingots, Korean silver vases, the silver of East and South-East Asian trade. Half a mace a day is a guess.

currencies.name: cowrie shells
currencies.note: Shang and Zhou cowrie money (shells and bronze imitations), counted in strings. Guesses.

currencies.name: Hong Kong dollar
currencies.note: From 1863 (Spanish and Mexican dollars before). Guesses.

currencies.name: Korean mun
currencies.note: Sangpyeong tongbo cash from 1678: nyang = 10 jeon = 100 mun. Guesses.

currencies.name: Korean yen
currencies.note: 1910-1945, at par with the Japanese yen. Guesses.

currencies.name: North Korean won
currencies.note: From 2009 (100 old; market prices rose far beyond the official ones). Guesses.

currencies.name: Vietnamese cash
currencies.note: Copper (later zinc) cash, 600 to the string (quan), 60 to the tien, from 970 to 1948. Guesses.

currencies.name: North Vietnamese đồng
currencies.note: Democratic Republic of Vietnam, 1946-1978 (the 1951 change of 100 to 1 is followed roughly).

currencies.name: Vietnamese đồng
currencies.note: Unified dong from 1978 (the 1985 change of 10 to 1 roughly). Guesses.

currencies.name: Cambodian riel
currencies.note: 1955-1975 and from 1980 (no money under the Khmer Rouge). Guesses.

currencies.name: Cambodian tical
currencies.note: Cambodian coins on the Siamese pattern, 1847-1884. Guesses.

currencies.name: Siamese tical
currencies.note: Silver bullet money (pod duang, flat coins from 1860): 1 baht = 4 salueng = 8 fueang = 64 att, 1 att = 100 bia (cowrie shells); 1 tamlueng = 4 baht. Wages are guesses.

currencies.name: Spanish dollar
currencies.note: Spanish and Mexican silver dollars, the trade money of Malaya, Borneo and the China coast; reckoned in 100 cents in the Straits. Guesses.

currencies.name: Malayan dollar
currencies.note: Malayan dollar, then the Malaya and British Borneo dollar, 1939-1967. Guesses.

currencies.name: Brunei dollar
currencies.note: From 1967 (at par with the Singapore dollar).

currencies.name: Sarawak dollar
currencies.note: Sarawak and North Borneo dollars, 1858-1953. Guesses.

currencies.name: Javanese mas
currencies.note: Gold and silver pieces by weight: tahil = 16 mas = 64 kupang. Guesses.

currencies.name: Philippine peso
currencies.note: Peso = 100 centimos/centavos from 1857 (8 reales before). Guesses.

currencies.name: made beaver
currencies.note: The Hudson's Bay Company's unit of trade: a prime beaver pelt; brass tokens of 1, 1/2, 1/4 and 1/8 made beaver (1854). Half a made beaver a day is a guess.

currencies.name: Canadian pound
currencies.note: Halifax currency: 1 pound = 4 Spanish dollars, 1764-1857. Guesses.

currencies.name: Hawaiian dollar
currencies.note: At par with the US dollar, 1847-1898. Guesses.

currencies.name: Central American peso
currencies.note: The peso of 8 reales of the Central American republics before their own currencies. Guesses.

currencies.name: Nicaraguan córdoba
currencies.note: From 1912 (the 1980s collapse and the cordoba oro of 1991 roughly). Guesses.

currencies.name: Panamanian balboa
currencies.note: From 1904, at par with the US dollar.

currencies.name: Cuban peso
currencies.note: Spanish Cuban peso, then the Cuban peso from 1915 (US dollars also used to 1951). Guesses.

currencies.name: Dominican peso
currencies.note: From 1844 (the US dollar 1905-1947 is folded in). Guesses.

currencies.name: British West Indies dollar
currencies.note: British West Indies dollar (1935) and British Caribbean dollar (1949-1965). Guesses.

currencies.name: Bahamian dollar
currencies.note: From 1966, at par with the US dollar.

currencies.name: Argentine peso
currencies.note: Peso fuerte and peso moneda nacional, to 1969. Guesses.

currencies.name: Argentine peso
currencies.note: Convertible peso from 1992 (10,000 australes); the later inflation roughly. Guesses.

currencies.name: Brazilian real (réis)
currencies.note: Colonial and imperial reis to 1942: the mil-reis of 1,000 reis, the conto of 1,000 mil-reis. Guesses.

currencies.name: Brazilian cruzeiro
currencies.note: 1990-1993 (at par with the cruzado novo). Guesses.

currencies.name: Guyanese dollar
currencies.note: British Guiana and Guyana dollar. Guesses.
